# Executive summary

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="What this analysis is doing and why"}

The CDR3-QTL analysis in [notebooks 01–04](AIRR_cdr3-QTL_04-cdr3riskscore.qmd) fit a position-specific motif model that links each CDR3-β amino-acid to a donor's cumulative Parkinson's-disease HLA-risk-allele dosage. The result is a **continuous per-CDR3 score** — a compact summary of how "HLA-risk-footprinted" a TCR-β is.

So far, that score has only been a donor-level readout, averaged over whole bulk repertoires. The question this report answers is **where that footprint actually lives inside a repertoire**: which T cell subtypes carry the HLA-risk CDR3 motifs, how clonal they are, how they differ between PD and HC, and whether high-risk-score cells within the same subtype have a distinct transcriptomic state from low-risk-score cells in the same donor.

We project the scoring function onto three external single-cell PD studies, harmonize cell-type annotations, score every CDR3-β at the single-cell level, and run both **subtype-level distribution tests** and **within-subtype within-PD differential expression** with donor modelled as a random intercept — the statistically conservative choice that most faithfully reflects the repeated-measures structure of the data.
:::

## Datasets

| Study | Compartment | Cells / CDR3s used here | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Wang et al. 2021** ([Cell Discovery](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41421-021-00280-3)) | Blood + CSF (10x 5' GEX + V(D)J) | ~81K T cells, 21 subtypes, 8 PD + 8 HC | **Primary** — all mechanistic follow-ups |
| **Ma et al. 2025** ([Nat Commun](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-62478-3)) | Post-mortem brain (SN + cortex) snRNA-seq + TCR-seq | 7,138 valid TRB CDR3s, 13 PD + 15 Ctrl | **Tissue comparator** — brain distribution |
| **Moquin-Beaudry et al. 2025** ([Brain](https://doi.org/10.1093/brain/awaf066)) | PBMC scRNA-seq + TCR-seq, 38 immune subtypes | pending public release | **Replication cohort** — template wired; data pending |

## Analytical strategy

1. **Ingest + harmonize** CDR3-β sequences across studies, keeping only IMGT-alignable lengths (12–18 AA).
2. **Score** every unique CDR3-β with the pre-computed CDR3-QTL beta-coefficients from notebook 04, across all phenotype variants, and join scores back to cell-level metadata.
3. **Map score distributions** across T cell subtypes to find where the high- and low-score CDR3s live (subtype-level).
4. **Dissect PD-specific signal** in Wang blood through four focused follow-ups: donor-level coupling, clonal-expansion stratification, CD8 trajectory / transition, and differential expression between high- and low-score cells within each PD subtype.
5. **Model differential expression with MAST + donor random intercept**, retaining all features (including TCR V/J/C genes, which carry legitimate cell-type biology), dropping uninformative score = 0 cells, and using a per-subtype median split on the full non-zero score distribution.

# Study 1 — Wang et al. 2021 (blood + CSF)

Wang et al. 2021 ([Cell Discovery](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41421-021-00280-3)) paired 10x Chromium 5' GEX with V(D)J TCR sequencing on sorted T cells from peripheral blood and CSF of 8 PD + 8 HC donors. It is the **only study in the field** with ~80K paired-chain TCRs, dense cell-type annotations across 21 CD4/CD8/γδ/Treg subtypes, and HLA typing for every donor — exactly the inputs this analysis needs. All mechanistic follow-ups downstream are anchored in Wang.

::: {.callout-note icon=false title="Dataset sources"}

- **Zenodo [record 3993994](https://zenodo.org/record/3993994)** — `counts.rds` (382 MB raw counts), `normalized.rds` (417 MB log-normalized), `metadata.txt` (16 MB cell annotations with CDR3 + cell-type labels), `README.txt`.
- **GEO [GSE134578](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE134578)** — CSF TCR data originally deposited by Gate et al. and reused in Wang 2021.
:::

## Download Wang et al. 2021 data

```{r download-wang}
zenodo_base <- "https://zenodo.org/record/3993994/files"
wang_files <- c("counts.rds", "normalized.rds", "metadata.txt", "README.txt")

for (f in wang_files) {
    dest <- glue("{wang_dir}/{f}")
    if (!file.exists(dest)) {
        message(glue("Downloading {f} via curl..."))
        exit_code <- system2("curl",
            args = c("-L", "-o", shQuote(dest),
                     "--retry", "3",
                     "--retry-delay", "5",
                     "-C", "-",
                     shQuote(glue("{zenodo_base}/{f}"))),
            stdout = "", stderr = ""
        )
        if (exit_code != 0) {
            warning(glue("curl failed for {f} (exit code {exit_code})"))
            if (file.exists(dest)) file.remove(dest)
        }
    } else {
        message(glue("{f} already exists, skipping."))
    }
}

# Verify downloads
wang_downloaded <- file.info(list.files(wang_dir, full.names = TRUE))
wang_downloaded$file <- basename(rownames(wang_downloaded))
wang_downloaded %>% dplyr::select(file, size) %>% print()

```

```{r load-wang-metadata}
wang_meta <- read.delim(glue("{wang_dir}/metadata.txt"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%

message(glue("Wang et al. 2021: {nrow(wang_meta)} cells"))
wang_meta %>% glimpse()

wang_meta %>% colnames() %>% sort() %>% print()
```

```{r wang-extract-cdr3b}
# Inspect TCR-related columns
wang_meta %>%

    colnames() %>%
    print()

    dplyr::select(matches("cluster|cell.?type|subtype|annotation|ident", ignore.case = TRUE)) %>%
    colnames() %>%

    colnames() %>%

```


```{r wang-clean-cdr3b}

wang_cdr3b <- wang_meta %>%
    mutate(condition = strex::str_before_first(sample_type, "\\(")) %>% 
    mutate(condition = gsub("MCI", "PD", condition)) %>% 
    mutate(condition = gsub("Parkinson", "PD", condition)) %>% 
    mutate(tissue = case_when(
        grepl("CSF", sample_type) ~ "CSF",
        grepl("Blood", sample_type) ~ "Blood",
        TRUE ~ "ERROR"
    )) %>% 
    rename(
        cdr3b_aa = beta_cdr3_aa,
        t_cell_subtype = cell_type2,
        donor_id = sample
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(cdr3b_aa) & cdr3b_aa != "") %>%
    filter(nchar(cdr3b_aa) >= 12 & nchar(cdr3b_aa) <= 18) %>%
    mutate(
        study = "Wang_2021",
        compartment = tissue
    ) %>%
    glimpse()

# CDR3 length distribution
wang_cdr3b %>%
    mutate(cdr3_len = nchar(cdr3b_aa)) %>%
    dplyr::count(cdr3_len) %>%
    print()

# T cell subtype breakdown
wang_cdr3b %>%
    dplyr::count(t_cell_subtype, sort = TRUE) %>%
    print()

# Condition breakdown
wang_cdr3b %>%
    dplyr::count(condition) %>%
    print()

```



# Study 2 — Moquin-Beaudry et al. 2025 (PBMC, pending)

This PBMC atlas — 78,876 cells across 38 immune subtypes from 14 PD + 6 atypical Parkinsonism + 10 HC donors ([Brain, 2025](https://doi.org/10.1093/brain/awaf066)) — is the natural replication cohort. As of the last check, the GEO accession is not yet public (PMC embargo until 2026-05-26). The scaffolding below is wired and commented; once GEO is indexed, uncommenting the three TODO chunks plus the line in the harmonization step will fold Moquin-Beaudry into every downstream analysis with no further edits.

scRNA-seq + TCR-seq of sorted PBMCs from 14 PD + 6 atypical Parkinsonism + 10 HC donors. 78,876 cells across 38 immune subtypes. Shared TCR clones identified across PD patients. Published in [Brain](https://doi.org/10.1093/brain/awaf066); preprint: [bioRxiv 10.1101/2024.07.26.605020](https://doi.org/10.1101/2024.07.26.605020).

# Study 4 — Ma et al. 2025 (post-mortem brain)

Ma et al. 2025 ([Nat Commun](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-62478-3)) profiled ~207K nuclei from post-mortem substantia nigra and cortex of 13 PD + 15 control brains, with a matched TCR-seq layer on sorted T-cell fractions. T cells are rare in brain parenchyma (535 T cells in PD SN), but this is the **only tissue dataset** with paired CDR3-β sequence + cell-type context we can project the risk score onto. Ma provides the brain-vs-blood comparator.

## Download Ma et al. 2025 data

Processed data and supplementary materials deposited on Zenodo:

- [Processed data](https://zenodo.org/records/19454950) — `data.zip` (6.7GB): snRNA-seq processed objects
- [Supplementary data](https://zenodo.org/records/19457732) — `SupplementaryData.zip` (105MB): supplementary tables
- [GitHub](https://github.com/dalhoomist/T-cell_and_glial_pathology_in_PD): analysis code

```{r download-ma}
# -- Processed data (6.7 GB) --
ma_data_zip <- glue("{ma_dir}/data.zip")
if (!file.exists(ma_data_zip)) {
    message("Downloading Ma et al. 2025 processed data (6.7 GB)...")
    system2("curl",
        args = c("-L", "-o", shQuote(ma_data_zip),
                 "--retry", "3", "--retry-delay", "5", "-C", "-",
                 shQuote("https://zenodo.org/records/19454950/files/data.zip")),
        stdout = "", stderr = ""
    )
} else {
    message("data.zip already exists, skipping.")
}

# -- Supplementary data (105 MB) --
ma_supp_zip <- glue("{ma_dir}/SupplementaryData.zip")
if (!file.exists(ma_supp_zip)) {
    message("Downloading Ma et al. 2025 supplementary data (105 MB)...")
    system2("curl",
        args = c("-L", "-o", shQuote(ma_supp_zip),
                 "--retry", "3", "--retry-delay", "5", "-C", "-",
                 shQuote("https://zenodo.org/records/19457732/files/SupplementaryData.zip")),
        stdout = "", stderr = ""
    )
} else {
    message("SupplementaryData.zip already exists, skipping.")
}

# Verify downloads
file.info(c(ma_data_zip, ma_supp_zip)) %>%
    mutate(file = basename(rownames(.))) %>%
    dplyr::select(file, size) %>%
    print()
```
