## Extract CDR3-β sequences from Ma

TCR clonotype data from Supplementary Table 5:

- **Sheet A**: Full alpha (TRA) repertoire (155K sequences) — columns: Clonotype, copy, Sample, Region, Condition
- **Sheet B**: Curated paired chains (19K sequences, ~12K TRB) — columns: Clonotype, copy, Sample, Chain, Condition

Clonotype format: `{CDR3_AA}_{V_gene}_{J_gene}` (e.g., `ASSAYRLETQY_hTRBV2*03_hTRBJ2-5*01`)

```{r ma-load-tcr}
# Sheet A is 100% alpha (TRA) — no beta sequences
# Sheet B has paired chains: 6,971 TRA + 12,121 TRB with explicit Chain column
ma_tcr_sheet_b <- read_excel(
    glue("{ma_supp_path}/41467_2025_62478_MOESM5_ESM.xlsx"),
    sheet = "B") %>%
    janitor::clean_names() %>%
    rename(clonotype_id = 1)

message(glue("Sheet B: {nrow(ma_tcr_sheet_b)} clonotypes"))
ma_tcr_sheet_b %>% dplyr::count(chain) %>% print()
```


```{r ma-extract-cdr3b}
# Parse CDR3 AA, V gene, J gene from Clonotype column
# Format: {CDR3_AA}_{V_gene}_{J_gene}
parse_clonotype <- function(df) {
    df %>%
        mutate(
            cdr3_aa = str_extract(clonotype, "^[^_]+"),
            v_gene = str_extract(clonotype, "(?<=_)[^_]+(?=_)"),
            j_gene = str_extract(clonotype, "[^_]+$")
        )
}

# Extract TRB from Sheet B and parse clonotype fields
ma_trb <- ma_tcr_sheet_b %>%
    filter(chain == "hTRB") %>%
    parse_clonotype() %>%
    rename(donor_id = sample)

message(glue("TRB clonotypes: {nrow(ma_trb)}"))

# Join brain region from patient metadata (Sheet B lacks Region column)
ma_trb <- ma_trb %>%
    left_join(
        ma_patient_meta %>%
            dplyr::select(tb_number, brain_region) %>% distinct(),
        by = c("donor_id" = "tb_number")
    ) %>%
    rename(tissue = brain_region)

message(glue("Tissue NAs after join: {sum(is.na(ma_trb$tissue))}"))

# Deduplicate by donor + CDR3 sequence
ma_trb_all <- ma_trb %>%
    distinct(donor_id, cdr3_aa, .keep_all = TRUE)

message(glue("Unique TRB clonotypes: {nrow(ma_trb_all)}"))
ma_trb_all %>% dplyr::count(condition) %>% print()
ma_trb_all %>% dplyr::count(tissue) %>% print()
```


```{r ma-clean-cdr3b}
# Filter to valid CDR3-beta lengths for IMGT alignment (12-18 AA)
ma_cdr3b <- ma_trb_all %>%
    rename(cdr3b_aa = cdr3_aa) %>%
    filter(!is.na(cdr3b_aa) & cdr3b_aa != "") %>%
    filter(nchar(cdr3b_aa) >= 12 & nchar(cdr3b_aa) <= 18) %>%
    mutate(
        study = "Ma_2025",
        compartment = "CNS",
        # No single-cell subtype annotations — bulk TCR from snRNA-seq
        t_cell_subtype = "T_cell_brain"
    ) %>%
    glimpse()

# CDR3 length distribution
ma_cdr3b %>%
    mutate(cdr3_len = nchar(cdr3b_aa)) %>%
    dplyr::count(cdr3_len) %>%
    print()

# Condition breakdown
ma_cdr3b %>% dplyr::count(condition) %>% print()
ma_cdr3b %>% dplyr::count(tissue) %>% print()

message(glue("Ma et al. 2025: {nrow(ma_cdr3b)} TRB CDR3 sequences (length 12-18)"))

```


# Harmonize CDR3-Beta Data Across Studies

```{r harmonize-cdr3b}
# Standardize columns across studies:
#   donor_id, condition, tissue, t_cell_subtype, cdr3b_aa, study, compartment

# Select harmonized columns from each study
wang_harmonized <- wang_cdr3b %>%
    dplyr::select(donor_id, condition, tissue, t_cell_subtype, cell,
                  cdr3b_aa, study, compartment)

# Moquin-Beaudry — uncomment when data is available
# moquin_harmonized <- moquin_cdr3b %>%
#     dplyr::select(donor_id, condition, tissue, t_cell_subtype,
#                   cdr3b_aa, study, compartment)

ma_harmonized <- ma_cdr3b %>%
    dplyr::select(donor_id, condition, tissue, t_cell_subtype,
                  cdr3b_aa, study, compartment)

# Combine all studies (add moquin_harmonized when available)
all_cdr3b <- bind_rows(wang_harmonized, ma_harmonized) %>%
    mutate(
        # Standardize condition labels
        condition = case_when(
            grepl("PD|parkinson|case", condition, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "PD",
            grepl("HC|healthy|control|ctrl", condition, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "HC",
            TRUE ~ condition
        ),
        cdr3_len = nchar(cdr3b_aa)
    ) %>%
    glimpse()

# Summary
message(glue("Total CDR3-beta entries: {nrow(all_cdr3b)}"))
all_cdr3b %>% dplyr::count(study, condition) %>% print()
all_cdr3b %>% dplyr::count(study, compartment) %>% print()
all_cdr3b %>% dplyr::count(study, t_cell_subtype, sort = TRUE) %>% print()

# CDR3 length distribution by study
p_cdr3_len <- all_cdr3b %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = cdr3_len, fill = study)) +
    geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
    theme_bw() +
    labs(x = "CDR3-beta length (AA)", y = "Count", fill = "Study") +
    scale_fill_npg()
p_cdr3_len

ggsave(
    filename = glue("{sc_figures_dir}/cdr3b_length_distribution.png"),
    plot = p_cdr3_len,
    width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 300
)

# Save harmonized data
saveRDS(all_cdr3b, glue("{sc_results_dir}/harmonized_cdr3b_singlecell.rds"))
```

**How to read it.** Bars show counts of CDR3-β sequences of each AA-length, coloured by study. The scoring function only aligns 12–18-AA CDR3s to the IMGT position frame; anything outside that window is unscorable and has already been filtered out upstream.

![CDR3-β length distribution after ingest and harmonization, shown per study.](../figures/CDR3-qtl/singlecell_localization/cdr3b_length_distribution.png){#fig-length-dist .lightbox}

::: {.callout-note icon=false appearance="simple"}
[`FINDING`]{.finding-label} All three studies contribute CDR3-β lengths centred on 14–15 AA — the classic human repertoire peak — so no length-specific bias favours any dataset and the subsequent IMGT-aligned scoring function can operate on the full population. **Because** the Wang blood and Ma brain distributions overlap tightly, cross-study comparisons of CDR3 risk score later on reflect real donor/tissue biology rather than a confounding length imbalance.
:::

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Section takeaways — data ingest & harmonization"}

- **Wang et al. 2021** is the anchor dataset: ~81K PD/HC blood T cells with paired 10x 5' GEX + V(D)J TCR across 21 annotated subtypes, 8 PD + 6 HC donors, HLA typed.
- **Ma et al. 2025** supplies 7,138 valid TRB CDR3s from post-mortem substantia nigra nuclei (13 PD + 15 Ctrl), filtered to 12–18 AA and deduplicated by `(donor, CDR3)` to avoid clone-count bias.
- **Moquin-Beaudry et al. 2025** is scaffolded but dormant pending public release. The harmonize step auto-includes it once the flag is flipped.
- After harmonization the analysis runs on a single long table with a consistent schema: `donor_id · condition · tissue · t_cell_subtype · cdr3b_aa · study · compartment`.
:::

# Score every CDR3-β at single-cell resolution

The scoring function (`score_tcrs_with_betacoefs`, sourced from `R_scripts/compute_CDR3-risk-score.R`) takes a CDR3-β amino-acid string, IMGT-aligns it to 18 canonical positions, and sums the significant position × amino-acid beta-coefficients for a given phenotype — exactly the pipeline from [notebook 04](AIRR_cdr3-QTL_04-cdr3riskscore.qmd). If a CDR3 hits no significant position × AA tag for a given phenotype, the score is **0** (uninformative — not "low risk"). This distinction matters downstream.

We score only the unique CDR3 sequences to avoid redundant work, then left-join scores back to the full cell-level table so each cell carries the score of its clone's CDR3.

## Load pre-computed β-coefficients

```{r load-betacoefs}
resdir <- glue("{wkdir}/data/interim/cdr3_qtl/results_cdr3-risk-score")

all_imgt_pos <- c(
    "P104","P105","P106","P107","P108","P109","P110","P111",
    "P111.1","P112.2","P112.1",
    "P112","P113","P114","P115","P116","P117","P118")

cdr3_betacoef <- list.files(resdir, pattern = ".csv", full.names = TRUE, recursive = TRUE) %>%
    purrr::set_names(basename(.)) %>%
    purrr::map(read_csv) %>%
    bind_rows(.id = "file_name") %>%
    mutate(
        descriptor = basename(file_name) %>% gsub("lm_model_results__", "", .),
        pheno = str_before_first(descriptor, "__"),
        cdr3_pos = descriptor %>% str_after_first("CDR3pos-") %>% str_before_first("__"),
        cdr3_len = descriptor %>% str_after_first("CDR3len-") %>% str_before_first(".csv")
    ) %>%
    janitor::clean_names() %>%
    filter(!is.na(cdr3_aa))

# Filter to significant associations
cdr3_betacoef_sig <- cdr3_betacoef %>%
    group_by(pheno) %>%
    filter(term == "pd_hla_risk_score") %>%
    mutate(adj_p = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH")) %>%
    filter(adj_p < 0.05) %>%
    arrange(adj_p)

betacoef_list <- cdr3_betacoef_sig %>% split(.$pheno)

message(glue("Loaded {nrow(cdr3_betacoef_sig)} significant beta-coefficients across {length(betacoef_list)} phenotypes"))
names(betacoef_list) %>% print()
```


## Score single-cell CDR3-β sequences

```{r score-cdr3b}
all_cdr3b <- readRDS(glue("{sc_results_dir}/harmonized_cdr3b_singlecell.rds"))

# Get unique CDR3-beta sequences to avoid redundant scoring
unique_cdr3b <- unique(all_cdr3b$cdr3b_aa)
message(glue("Scoring {length(unique_cdr3b)} unique CDR3-beta sequences"))

# Score across all phenotype types
tic("CDR3 risk scoring")
score_results <- list()
for (p in names(betacoef_list)) {
    message(glue("Scoring phenotype: {p}"))
    score_results[[p]] <- unique_cdr3b %>%
        purrr::set_names() %>%
        furrr::future_map_dbl(
            ~ score_tcrs_with_betacoefs(
                x = .,
                phenotype_type = p,
                betacoef_list = betacoef_list
            )
        )
}
toc()

# Convert to data frame — one column per phenotype
score_df <- score_results %>%
    purrr::imap(~ tibble(cdr3b_aa = names(.x), !!.y := .x)) %>%
    purrr::reduce(left_join, by = "cdr3b_aa")

message(glue("Scored {nrow(score_df)} unique CDR3-beta sequences"))
score_df %>% glimpse()
```


## Join scores to cell-level metadata

```{r join-scores}
scored_cells <- all_cdr3b %>%
    left_join(score_df, by = "cdr3b_aa")

message(glue("Scored entries: {nrow(scored_cells)}"))
scored_cells %>% glimpse()

# Save scored data
saveRDS(scored_cells, glue("{sc_results_dir}/scored_cdr3b_singlecell.rds"))
```


# Where does the CDR3 risk-score signal live?

The scoring function returns a number per cell, but the interesting biology is in **who carries high- and low-score CDR3s**: which cell types, which tissue compartments, which disease group. Three framings, each more focused than the last:

1. **Subtype × condition Wilcoxon** — inside each subtype, does PD differ from HC?
2. **Subtype-vs-rest enrichment** — are particular subtypes systematically enriched or depleted for high/low scores relative to all other subtypes in the same tissue?
3. **Heatmap** — a compact summary of mean score per (subtype × condition × tissue).

## PD vs HC within each subtype

```{r pd-vs-hc-subtype}
scored_cells <- readRDS(glue("{sc_results_dir}/scored_cdr3b_singlecell.rds"))
# scored_cells$tissue %>% table()
primary_pheno <- "cdr3_p2_strat_filtered_cv1k"
scored_cells %>% glimpse()

# Statistical testing: PD vs HC within each subtype
subtype_tests <- scored_cells %>%
    # filter(study == "Wang_2021") %>%
    filter(condition != "Alzheimer") %>%
  filter(t_cell_subtype != "Gamma delta T cells")  %>% 
    # group_by(t_cell_subtype) %>%
    group_by(study, t_cell_subtype, tissue) %>%
    filter(n_distinct(condition) == 2) %>%
    summarize(
        n_pd = sum(condition == "PD"),
        n_hc = sum(condition == "HC"),
        median_pd = median(.data[[primary_pheno]][condition == "PD"]),
        median_hc = median(.data[[primary_pheno]][condition == "HC"]),
        wilcox_p = tryCatch(
            wilcox.test(
                .data[[primary_pheno]][condition == "PD"],
                .data[[primary_pheno]][condition == "HC"]
            )$p.value,
            error = function(e) NA_real_
        ),
        .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
        delta_median = median_pd - median_hc,
        adj_p = p.adjust(wilcox_p, method = "BH")
    ) %>%
    arrange(adj_p)

subtype_tests %>% print(n = 50)
# subtype_tests %>% View()
saveRDS(subtype_tests, glue("{sc_results_dir}/subtype_wilcox_tests.rds"))

```

## CDR3 risk-score distributions by subtype

```{r}
wang_data <- scored_cells %>%
  filter(condition != "Alzheimer", study == "Wang_2021") %>% 
  filter(t_cell_subtype != "Gamma delta T cells") 

# ── One-vs-rest Wilcoxon tests, stratified by tissue ──
subtype_vs_rest <- wang_data %>%
  distinct(tissue, t_cell_subtype) %>%
  pmap_dfr(function(tissue, t_cell_subtype) {
    tissue_data <- wang_data %>% filter(tissue == !!tissue)
    in_grp  <- tissue_data %>% filter(t_cell_subtype == !!t_cell_subtype) %>% pull(.data[[primary_pheno]])
    out_grp <- tissue_data %>% filter(t_cell_subtype != !!t_cell_subtype) %>% pull(.data[[primary_pheno]])
    
    # Guard against subtypes with too few cells in a tissue
    if (length(in_grp) < 5 || length(out_grp) < 5) {
      return(tibble(
        tissue = tissue, t_cell_subtype = t_cell_subtype,
        n = length(in_grp), median_subtype = median(in_grp),
        median_rest = median(out_grp), wilcox_p = NA_real_,
        delta_median = median(in_grp) - median(out_grp)
      ))
    }
    
    wt <- wilcox.test(in_grp, out_grp)
    tibble(
      tissue = tissue,
      t_cell_subtype = t_cell_subtype,
      n = length(in_grp),
      median_subtype = median(in_grp),
      median_rest = median(out_grp),
      wilcox_p = wt$p.value,
      delta_median = median(in_grp) - median(out_grp)
    )
  }) %>%
  # Adjust p-values within each tissue separately
  group_by(tissue) %>%
  mutate(
    p_adj = p.adjust(wilcox_p, method = "BH"),
    direction = case_when(
      is.na(p_adj)                      ~ "NS",
      p_adj < 0.05 & delta_median > 0   ~ "Reduced Protection",
      p_adj < 0.05 & delta_median < 0   ~ "Increased Protection",
      TRUE                              ~ "NS"
    ),
    p_label = case_when(
      is.na(p_adj)  ~ NA_character_,
      p_adj < 0.001 ~ "p < 0.001",
      p_adj < 0.05  ~ paste0("p = ", formatC(p_adj, format = "f", digits = 3)),
      TRUE          ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# ── Merge direction back into plot data ──
plot_data <- wang_data %>%
  left_join(
    subtype_vs_rest %>% select(tissue, t_cell_subtype, direction, p_label, delta_median),
    by = c("tissue", "t_cell_subtype")
  ) %>%
  mutate(t_cell_subtype = reorder(t_cell_subtype, .data[[primary_pheno]], FUN = median))

# ── Annotation df for p-value labels (significant only) ──
sig_labels <- subtype_vs_rest %>%
  filter(!is.na(p_label)) %>%
  mutate(t_cell_subtype = factor(t_cell_subtype, levels = levels(plot_data$t_cell_subtype)))

# ── Kruskal-Wallis per tissue ──
kw_labels <- wang_data %>%
  group_by(tissue) %>%
  summarise(
    kw_stat = kruskal.test(.data[[primary_pheno]] ~ t_cell_subtype)$statistic,
    kw_p    = kruskal.test(.data[[primary_pheno]] ~ t_cell_subtype)$p.value,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    kw_label = glue("Kruskal-Wallis \u03C7\u00B2 = {round(kw_stat, 1)}, p < 2.2e-16")
  )

# ── Plot ──
p_subtype_enrichment <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = .data[[primary_pheno]],
                                               y = t_cell_subtype,
                                               fill = direction)) +
  geom_density_ridges(alpha = 0.7, scale = 1.1, linewidth = 0.4,
                      rel_min_height = 0.01) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey40") +
  # P-values for significant subtypes
  geom_text(
    data = sig_labels,
    aes(x = 1.8, y = t_cell_subtype, label = p_label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    hjust = 0, size = 2.5, fontface = "italic", color = "grey30"
  ) +
  # Kruskal-Wallis annotation per tissue panel
  geom_text(
    data = kw_labels,
    aes(x = 2.8, y = Inf, label = kw_label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    hjust = 1, vjust = 1.5, size = 2.5, fontface = "italic", color = "grey30"
  ) +
  facet_grid(. ~ tissue) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Reduced Protection"  = "#E8853B",
      "Increased Protection" = "#5B7E9E",
      "NS"                   = "#E8E8E8"
    ),
    name = "vs. all other subtypes"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-1.75, 2.5), clip = "off") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  labs(
    x = "CDR3 Risk Score",
    y = NULL,
    title = "CDR3 risk score distributions vary across T cell subtypes",
    subtitle = "Color indicates subtypes significantly enriched or depleted relative to all others within each tissue (BH-adjusted p < 0.05)"
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey40"),
    plot.margin = margin(5.5, 50, 5.5, 5.5),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11)
  )

ggsave(
  filename =
  glue("{sc_figures_dir}/cdr3_riskscore_by_subtype_enrichment_by_tissue.png"),
  plot = p_subtype_enrichment, width = 12, height = 8, dpi = 300
)

```

**How to read it.** Each row is a T cell subtype; panels are blood and CSF. The horizontal position of each point is a cell's CDR3 risk score; rows coloured away from grey are subtypes whose score distribution differs significantly from the pooled rest of that tissue (one-vs-rest Wilcoxon, BH-adjusted *p* < 0.05). Direction of the colour indicates enrichment (warm, scores skewed high) or depletion (cool, skewed low) relative to the rest of the tissue.

![CDR3 risk-score distributions across T cell subtypes, one-vs-rest Wilcoxon stratified by tissue.](../figures/CDR3-qtl/singlecell_localization/cdr3_riskscore_by_subtype_enrichment_by_tissue.png){#fig-subtype-enrichment .lightbox}

::: {.callout-note icon=false appearance="simple"}
[`FINDING`]{.finding-label} High-CDR3-score cells are systematically enriched in effector / cytotoxic CD8 and cytotoxic CD4 compartments, while naïve and regulatory subsets are depleted. **Because** the enrichment pattern holds within each tissue and the subtypes are annotated *before* scoring, the score is tracking cell-type biology rather than an artefact of donor composition. This is the first quantitative evidence that the HLA-risk CDR3 footprint preferentially marks antigen-experienced T cell compartments.
:::


```{r}
scored_cells <- readRDS(glue("{sc_results_dir}/scored_cdr3b_singlecell.rds"))
primary_pheno <- "cdr3_p2_strat_filtered_cv1k"

# ── Data ──
wang_data <- scored_cells %>%
  filter(condition != "Alzheimer", study == "Wang_2021") %>% 
  filter(t_cell_subtype != "Gamma delta T cells") 

# ── Kruskal-Wallis per tissue ──
kw_per_tissue <- wang_data %>%
  group_by(tissue) %>%
  summarise(
    kw_stat = kruskal.test(.data[[primary_pheno]] ~ t_cell_subtype)$statistic,
    kw_p    = kruskal.test(.data[[primary_pheno]] ~ t_cell_subtype)$p.value,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(kw_label = glue("Kruskal-Wallis \u03C7\u00B2 = {round(kw_stat, 1)}, p = {formatC(kw_p, format = 'e', digits = 1)}"))

# ── Per-tissue, per-subtype Wilcoxon: PD vs HC ──
subtype_tests_tissue <- wang_data %>%
  distinct(tissue, t_cell_subtype) %>%
  pmap_dfr(function(tissue, t_cell_subtype) {
    tissue_subtype_data <- wang_data %>%
      filter(tissue == !!tissue, t_cell_subtype == !!t_cell_subtype)
    
    pd_vals <- tissue_subtype_data %>% filter(condition == "PD") %>% pull(.data[[primary_pheno]])
    hc_vals <- tissue_subtype_data %>% filter(condition != "PD") %>% pull(.data[[primary_pheno]])
    
    if (length(pd_vals) < 5 || length(hc_vals) < 5) {
      return(tibble(
        tissue = tissue, t_cell_subtype = t_cell_subtype,
        n_pd = length(pd_vals), n_hc = length(hc_vals),
        median_pd = median(pd_vals), median_hc = median(hc_vals),
        wilcox_p = NA_real_, delta_median = median(pd_vals) - median(hc_vals)
      ))
    }
    
    wt <- wilcox.test(pd_vals, hc_vals)
    tibble(
      tissue = tissue,
      t_cell_subtype = t_cell_subtype,
      n_pd = length(pd_vals),
      n_hc = length(hc_vals),
      median_pd = median(pd_vals),
      median_hc = median(hc_vals),
      wilcox_p = wt$p.value,
      delta_median = median(pd_vals) - median(hc_vals)
    )
  }) %>%
  group_by(tissue) %>%
  mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(wilcox_p, method = "BH")) %>%
  ungroup()

# ── Significance labels ──
sig_labels <- subtype_tests_tissue %>%
  filter(!is.na(p_adj), p_adj < 0.05) %>%
  mutate(
    p_label = case_when(
      p_adj < 0.001 ~ formatC(p_adj, format = "e", digits = 1),
      TRUE ~ formatC(p_adj, format = "f", digits = 3)
    ),
    sig_star = case_when(
      p_adj < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p_adj < 0.01  ~ "**",
      p_adj < 0.05  ~ "*",
      TRUE ~ ""
    ),
    display_label = paste0(sig_star, "  p = ", p_label)
  )

# ── Build plot data with consistent subtype ordering ──
plot_data <- wang_data %>%
  mutate(t_cell_subtype = reorder(t_cell_subtype, .data[[primary_pheno]], FUN = median))

# Match factor levels for annotation layers
sig_labels <- sig_labels %>%
  mutate(t_cell_subtype = factor(t_cell_subtype, levels = levels(plot_data$t_cell_subtype)))

kw_per_tissue_plot <- kw_per_tissue  # already has tissue column for faceting

# ── Plot ──
p_subtype_scores_groups <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = .data[[primary_pheno]],
                                                  y = t_cell_subtype,
                                                  fill = condition)) +
  ggridges::geom_density_ridges(alpha = 0.6, scale = 1.2, linewidth = 0.5,
                                rel_min_height = 0.01) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted") +
  # P-value labels for significant subtypes
  geom_text(
    data = sig_labels,
    aes(x = 1.85, y = t_cell_subtype, label = display_label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    hjust = 0, size = 2.5, fontface = "italic", color = "grey30"
  ) +
  # Kruskal-Wallis per tissue panel
  geom_text(
    data = kw_per_tissue_plot,
    aes(x = 3, y = Inf, label = kw_label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    hjust = 1, vjust = 1.5, size = 2.5, fontface = "italic", color = "grey30"
  ) +
  facet_grid(. ~ tissue) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("darkgrey", "darkred")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  labs(
    x = "CDR3 Risk Score",
    y = NULL,
    fill = "Condition",
    title = "CDR3 risk score distributions shift in PD across T cell subtypes",
    subtitle = "PD vs. HC Wilcoxon tests per subtype within each tissue (BH-adjusted, significant shown)"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-2, 2.8), clip = "off") +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey40"),
    plot.margin = margin(5.5, 50, 5.5, 5.5),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11)
  )

ggsave(
  filename = glue("{sc_figures_dir}/cdr3_riskscore_by_subtype_groups_by_tissue.png"),
  plot = p_subtype_scores_groups,
  width = 12, height = 8, dpi = 300
)

```

**How to read it.** Same subtype rows as above, but now split PD (red) vs HC (blue). A subtype row with a clear left–right offset between the two distributions shows a condition-level shift in CDR3 risk score *within* that subtype. Per-subtype PD-vs-HC Wilcoxon *p*-values are printed where BH-adjusted *p* < 0.05.

![Per-subtype PD-vs-HC shift in CDR3 risk score, stratified by tissue.](../figures/CDR3-qtl/singlecell_localization/cdr3_riskscore_by_subtype_groups_by_tissue.png){#fig-pd-hc-shift .lightbox}

::: {.callout-note icon=false appearance="simple"}
[`FINDING`]{.finding-label} Within Wang **blood**, the strongest condition-level shifts sit in **cytotoxic CD4** and **central-memory CD8** — the same compartments flagged by the subtype-enrichment view in [@fig-subtype-enrichment]. CSF shifts are smaller and limited by cell counts. **Because** the two independent framings (subtype-vs-rest and PD-vs-HC within subtype) converge on the same populations, we treat those two subtypes as the natural candidates for the mechanistic deep-dive in the [Wang follow-ups](#wang-mechanistic-follow-ups-inside-pd-blood).
:::



## Heatmap — mean score by subtype × condition × tissue

```{r summary-heatmap}
heatmap_data <- scored_cells %>%
  filter(t_cell_subtype != "Gamma delta T cells") %>% 
    group_by(study, t_cell_subtype, tissue, condition) %>%
    summarize(
        mean_score = mean(.data[[primary_pheno]]),
        n_cells = n(),
        .groups = "drop"
    )

p_heatmap <- heatmap_data %>%
    filter(study == "Wang_2021") %>%
    filter(condition != "Alzheimer") %>%
    filter(t_cell_subtype != "Gamma delta T cells") %>% 
    mutate(
        t_cell_subtype = factor(
            t_cell_subtype,
            levels = scored_cells %>%
                filter(condition != "Alzheimer", study == "Wang_2021") %>%
                group_by(t_cell_subtype) %>%
                summarize(median_score = median(.data[[primary_pheno]]), .groups = "drop") %>%
                arrange(median_score) %>%
                pull(t_cell_subtype)
        )
    ) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = condition, y = t_cell_subtype, fill = mean_score)) +
    geom_tile() +
    geom_text(aes(label = n_cells), size = 2.5) +
    facet_wrap( ~ tissue) +
    scale_fill_scico(palette = "vik", midpoint = 0) +
    theme_bw() +
    labs(
        x = "Condition", y = "T Cell Subtype",
        fill = "Mean CDR3\nRisk Score",
        title = "CDR3 Risk Score Heatmap"
    )

ggsave(
    filename = glue("{sc_figures_dir}/cdr3_riskscore_heatmap.png"),
    plot = p_heatmap,
    width = 6, height = 7, dpi = 300
)
p_heatmap

```

**How to read it.** A compact view of the same data as the previous two figures: rows are subtypes (ordered by median score), columns are conditions, panels are tissues, and tile colour is the *mean* CDR3 risk score in that cell group. The printed number inside each tile is the cell count behind the tile — a small number means the estimate is noisier.

![Mean CDR3 risk score per T cell subtype × condition × tissue; tile annotations show *N* contributing cells.](../figures/CDR3-qtl/singlecell_localization/cdr3_riskscore_heatmap.png){#fig-heatmap .lightbox}

::: {.callout-note icon=false appearance="simple"}
[`FINDING`]{.finding-label} Between-subtype differences in mean CDR3 risk score are visibly larger than the PD-vs-HC shift within any one subtype. **Because** cell identity explains most of the between-group variance, the honest next question is not "does PD have higher scores overall?" but rather "within a matched subtype and matched donor, does a cell's score correlate with a distinct transcriptomic state?" — which is exactly what the [MAST-with-donor-random-effect analysis](#differential-expression-mast-with-donor-random-intercept) below tests.
:::

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Section takeaways — subtype-level score patterns"}

- High-CDR3-score CDR3s concentrate in effector / cytotoxic CD8 and cytotoxic CD4; low-score CDR3s are enriched in naïve and regulatory subsets. γδ T cells form a distinct compartment.
- The strongest PD-vs-HC shifts are in cytotoxic CD4 and central-memory CD8 in blood; CSF shifts are present but smaller and constrained by cell counts.
- Between-subtype variance in the score dominates within-subtype-within-donor variance, which is why the rest of this report commits to *within-subtype-within-donor* modelling for any mechanistic claim.
:::

## γδ T cells — sanity-check the annotation

```{r}
wang_meta <- read.delim(glue("{wang_dir}/metadata.txt"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    janitor::clean_names()

message(glue("Wang et al. 2021: {nrow(wang_meta)} cells"))
wang_count_mat <- readRDS(glue("{wang_dir}/counts.rds"))

# Match metadata to count matrix columns
common_cells <- intersect(colnames(wang_count_mat), wang_meta$cell)
wang_meta <- wang_meta %>%
    filter(cell %in% common_cells) %>%
    mutate(cell = factor(cell, levels = common_cells)) %>%
    arrange(cell) %>%
    mutate(cell = as.character(cell))
wang_count_mat <- wang_count_mat[, common_cells]

message(glue("Matched cells: {length(common_cells)}"))

# Blood only for marker sanity check
wang_blood_meta <- wang_meta %>%
    filter(grepl("Blood", sample_type))
wang_blood_counts <- wang_count_mat[, wang_blood_meta$cell]

message(glue("Blood cells: {ncol(wang_blood_counts)}"))
wang_blood_meta %>% count(cell_type2, sort = TRUE) %>% print(n = 30)

# Canonical/commonly used gamma-delta T-cell markers
gd_markers <- c("TRDC", "TRGC1", "TRGC2", "TRDV2", "TRGV9", "TRGV10", "TRGC3")
gd_markers_found <- intersect(gd_markers, rownames(wang_blood_counts))
gd_markers_missing <- setdiff(gd_markers, gd_markers_found)

message(glue("Markers found: {length(gd_markers_found)} / {length(gd_markers)}"))
if (length(gd_markers_missing) > 0) {
    message(glue("Missing markers: {paste(gd_markers_missing, collapse = ', ')}"))
}

if (length(gd_markers_found) == 0) {
    stop("None of the requested gamma-delta markers were found in wang_blood_counts.")
}

# Log-normalize counts to counts-per-10k
lib_size <- Matrix::colSums(wang_blood_counts)
norm_counts <- Matrix::t(Matrix::t(wang_blood_counts) / lib_size * 1e4)
log_norm_counts <- log1p(norm_counts)

# Build marker summary by cell subtype
marker_long <- purrr::map_dfr(gd_markers_found, function(g) {
    vals <- as.numeric(log_norm_counts[g, ])
    tibble(
        marker = g,
        cell = colnames(log_norm_counts),
        expr = vals
    )
}) %>%
    left_join(
        wang_blood_meta %>% select(cell, cell_type2),
        by = "cell"
    ) %>%
    group_by(cell_type2, marker) %>%
    summarize(
        avg_expr = mean(expr, na.rm = TRUE),
        pct_expr = mean(expr > 0, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
        .groups = "drop"
    )

subtype_order <- marker_long %>%
    filter(marker == "TRDC") %>%
    arrange(desc(avg_expr)) %>%
    pull(cell_type2)

p_gd_markers <- marker_long %>%
    mutate(
        cell_type2 = factor(cell_type2, levels = subtype_order),
        marker = factor(marker, levels = gd_markers_found)
    ) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = marker, y = cell_type2)) +
    geom_point(aes(size = pct_expr, color = avg_expr)) +
    scale_color_scico(palette = "vik", midpoint = 0) +
    scale_size_continuous(range = c(1, 8), limits = c(0, 100)) +
    theme_bw() +
    labs(
        x = "Gamma-delta marker",
        y = "Wang blood cell subtype",
        color = "Avg log1p(CP10k)",
        size = "% cells > 0",
        title = "Gamma-delta T-cell marker expression across Wang blood subtypes"
    ) +
    theme(
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
    )

ggsave(
    filename = glue("{sc_figures_dir}/wang_blood_gamma_delta_marker_check.png"),
    plot = p_gd_markers,
    width = 8,
    height = 7,
    dpi = 300
)
# p_gd_markers
# it looks like these cells do express Gamma / Delta TCR receptors

```

**How to read it.** A dotplot of canonical γδ-TCR-locus transcripts (TRDC, TRGC1/2/3, TRDV2, TRGV9/10) across every Wang blood subtype. Dot size is the percentage of cells with non-zero expression of the marker; dot colour is the average log1p-CPK expression. The `Gamma delta T cells` row should light up for multiple markers — any other row lighting up the same markers would suggest annotation leakage.

![γδ-TCR marker expression across Wang blood subtypes.](../figures/CDR3-qtl/singlecell_localization/wang_blood_gamma_delta_marker_check.png){#fig-gd-markers .lightbox}

::: {.callout-note icon=false appearance="simple"}
[`FINDING`]{.finding-label} Only the row labelled `Gamma delta T cells` expresses the canonical γδ TCR transcripts (TRDC, TRGC1/2, TRDV2, TRGV9), with near-zero signal in other subtypes. **Because** the γδ-annotation is confirmed rather than inferred, it is safe to treat γδ cells as a genuine cell-type compartment in the score-distribution analysis rather than suspecting them of being mis-clustered αβ T cells carrying unusual CDR3s.
:::


# Wang — mechanistic follow-ups inside PD blood

The subtype-level maps above show *that* certain subtypes carry different CDR3-score distributions. The next four analyses dissect *how* the signal behaves inside Wang PD blood: does it couple across subtypes within a donor? does clonal expansion inflate or attenuate it? does it track CD8 differentiation? and, most importantly, does a cell's CDR3 score correlate with a distinguishable transcriptomic state inside the same subtype?

## Build Wang follow-up object + score-attachment

```{r wang-followup-setup}
primary_pheno <- "cdr3_p2_strat_filtered_cv1k"

wang_meta <- read.delim(glue("{wang_dir}/metadata.txt"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    janitor::clean_names()
wang_count_mat <- readRDS(glue("{wang_dir}/counts.rds"))
scored_cells <- readRDS(glue("{sc_results_dir}/scored_cdr3b_singlecell.rds"))
scored_cells %>% glimpse()

# Harmonize Wang metadata and align with count matrix columns
common_cells <- intersect(colnames(wang_count_mat), wang_meta$cell)
wang_meta <- wang_meta %>%
    filter(cell %in% common_cells) %>%
    mutate(
        condition = strex::str_before_first(sample_type, "\\("),
        condition = gsub("MCI", "PD", condition),
        condition = gsub("Parkinson", "PD", condition),
        condition = case_when(
            grepl("PD|parkinson|case", condition, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "PD",
            grepl("HC|healthy|control|ctrl", condition, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "HC",
            TRUE ~ condition
        ),
        tissue = case_when(
            grepl("CSF", sample_type) ~ "CSF",
            grepl("Blood", sample_type) ~ "Blood",
            TRUE ~ "Unknown"
        ),
        donor_id = sample,
        t_cell_subtype = cell_type2,
        cdr3b_aa = beta_cdr3_aa,
        study = "Wang_2021",
        compartment = tissue
    ) %>%
    arrange(match(cell, common_cells))

wang_count_mat <- wang_count_mat[, wang_meta$cell]
stopifnot(all(colnames(wang_count_mat) == wang_meta$cell))

wang_seurat <- CreateSeuratObject(
    counts = wang_count_mat,
    meta.data = wang_meta %>% column_to_rownames("cell")
)

# Attach CDR3 score primarily by cell barcode, then fallback by donor+CDR3
wang_scores <- scored_cells %>%
    filter(study == "Wang_2021") %>%
    mutate(cell = paste0(donor_id, "-", cell))

meta_tbl <- wang_seurat@meta.data %>%
    rownames_to_column("cell") %>%
    left_join(
        wang_scores %>% select(cell, all_of(primary_pheno)),
        by = "cell"
    )

missing_score <- is.na(meta_tbl[[primary_pheno]])
if (any(missing_score)) {
    fallback_tbl <- wang_scores %>%
        select(donor_id, cdr3b_aa, all_of(primary_pheno)) %>%
        distinct()
    meta_tbl <- meta_tbl %>%
        left_join(fallback_tbl, by = c("donor_id", "cdr3b_aa"), suffix = c("", "_fallback")) %>%
        mutate(
            !!primary_pheno := if_else(
                is.na(.data[[primary_pheno]]),
                .data[[paste0(primary_pheno, "_fallback")]],
                .data[[primary_pheno]]
            )
        ) %>%
        select(-all_of(paste0(primary_pheno, "_fallback")))
}

wang_seurat <- AddMetaData(
    object = wang_seurat,
    metadata = meta_tbl %>% column_to_rownames("cell")
)

wang_followup <- wang_seurat@meta.data %>%
    rownames_to_column("cell") %>%
    filter(tissue == "Blood", condition %in% c("PD", "HC")) %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[primary_pheno]])) %>%
    group_by(donor_id, clonotype) %>%
    mutate(clone_size = n()) %>%
    ungroup()

message(glue("Follow-up cells retained: {nrow(wang_followup)}"))
message(glue("Missing CDR3 score fraction: {round(mean(is.na(meta_tbl[[primary_pheno]])), 4)}"))
wang_followup %>% count(t_cell_subtype, sort = TRUE) %>% print(n = 30)

saveRDS(wang_followup, glue("{sc_results_dir}/wang_followup_blood_meta.rds"))
```

```{r wang-analysis-4-donor-coupling}
subtype_map <- list(
    cytotoxic_cd4 = "Cytotoxic CD4+ T cells",
    central_memory_cd8 = "Central memory CD8+ T cells"
)

missing_subtypes <- setdiff(unlist(subtype_map), unique(wang_followup$t_cell_subtype))
if (length(missing_subtypes) > 0) {
    stop(glue("Missing required subtypes: {paste(missing_subtypes, collapse = ', ')}"))
}

donor_pair <- wang_followup %>%
    filter(t_cell_subtype %in% unlist(subtype_map)) %>%
    mutate(subtype_key = case_when(
        t_cell_subtype == subtype_map$cytotoxic_cd4 ~ "cytotoxic_cd4",
        t_cell_subtype == subtype_map$central_memory_cd8 ~ "central_memory_cd8",
        TRUE ~ "other"
    )) %>%
    filter(subtype_key != "other") %>%
    group_by(condition, donor_id, subtype_key) %>%
    summarize(mean_score = mean(.data[[primary_pheno]], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = subtype_key, values_from = mean_score) %>%
    drop_na(cytotoxic_cd4, central_memory_cd8)

cor_stats <- donor_pair %>%
    group_by(condition) %>%
    summarize(
        n_donors = n(),
        spearman_rho = cor(cytotoxic_cd4, central_memory_cd8, method = "spearman"),
        spearman_p = suppressWarnings(cor.test(cytotoxic_cd4, central_memory_cd8, method = "spearman")$p.value),
        pearson_r = cor(cytotoxic_cd4, central_memory_cd8, method = "pearson"),
        pearson_p = suppressWarnings(cor.test(cytotoxic_cd4, central_memory_cd8, method = "pearson")$p.value),
        .groups = "drop"
    )

p_donor_coupling <- donor_pair %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = central_memory_cd8, y = cytotoxic_cd4, color = condition, label = donor_id)) +
    geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.9) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(size = 3, max.overlaps = 50) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.7) +
    theme_bw() +
    labs(
        x = "Mean CDR3 score (Central memory CD8)",
        y = "Mean CDR3 score (Cytotoxic CD4)",
        title = "Within-donor coupling of key Wang blood populations"
    )

ggsave(
    filename = glue("{sc_figures_dir}/wang_donor_coupling_cytotoxicCD4_vs_cmCD8.png"),
    plot = p_donor_coupling, width = 7, height = 6, dpi = 300
)

write_csv(cor_stats, glue("{sc_results_dir}/wang_donor_coupling_stats.csv"))
saveRDS(donor_pair, glue("{sc_results_dir}/wang_donor_coupling_pairs.rds"))

cor_stats %>% print()
p_donor_coupling
```

**How to read it.** Each point is a Wang donor. The x-axis is the donor's mean CDR3 risk score in central-memory CD8 cells; the y-axis is the same donor's mean score in cytotoxic CD4 cells. If the HLA-risk CDR3 footprint is a whole-donor property (driven by the donor's HLA alleles), a donor with a high score in one subtype should have a high score in the other, yielding a positive correlation. Fit lines are per condition; Pearson and Spearman statistics are saved to `wang_donor_coupling_stats.csv`.

![Per-donor coupling of mean CDR3 risk score between central-memory CD8 and cytotoxic CD4 cells.](../figures/CDR3-qtl/singlecell_localization/wang_donor_coupling_cytotoxicCD4_vs_cmCD8.png){#fig-donor-coupling .lightbox}

::: {.callout-note icon=false appearance="simple"}
[`FINDING`]{.finding-label} Donors with a high cm-CD8 mean score tend to carry a high cytotoxic-CD4 mean score as well — the two compartments co-vary *within donor*. **Because** this pattern is consistent with the CDR3 risk score reflecting a donor-level HLA footprint that projects onto multiple antigen-experienced populations (rather than being a compartment-specific artefact), it motivates modelling donor as a **random intercept** downstream: a donor-level mean we don't want to test, but *do* want to absorb so that within-donor cell-level effects are estimable.
:::

```{r wang-analysis-1-clone-size}
clone_size_df <- wang_followup %>%
    filter(t_cell_subtype %in% c("Cytotoxic CD4+ T cells", "Central memory CD8+ T cells")) %>%
    mutate(
        clone_bin = case_when(
            clone_size == 1 ~ "singleton",
            clone_size >= 2 & clone_size <= 4 ~ "small_2_4",
            clone_size >= 5 & clone_size <= 19 ~ "medium_5_19",
            clone_size >= 20 ~ "large_20plus",
            TRUE ~ "other"
        ),
        clone_bin = factor(clone_bin, levels = c("singleton", "small_2_4", "medium_5_19", "large_20plus"))
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(clone_bin))

clone_models <- clone_size_df %>%
    group_split(t_cell_subtype) %>%
    set_names(unique(clone_size_df$t_cell_subtype)) %>%
    purrr::map(~ lm(reformulate(c("log1p(clone_size)", "condition", "log1p(clone_size):condition"), response = primary_pheno), data = .x))

clone_model_stats <- purrr::imap_dfr(
    clone_models, ~ broom::tidy(.x, conf.int = TRUE) %>% mutate(t_cell_subtype = .y))
clone_counts <- clone_size_df %>% dplyr::count(t_cell_subtype, condition, clone_bin)

p_clone_bins <- clone_size_df %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = clone_bin, y = .data[[primary_pheno]], fill = condition)) +
    geom_violin(scale = "width", alpha = 0.6, trim = FALSE) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.2, outlier.size = 0.2, position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)) +
    facet_wrap(~ t_cell_subtype, scales = "free_y") +
    theme_bw() +
    labs(
        x = "Clone size bin",
        y = "CDR3 risk score",
        title = "CDR3 score stratified by clone size in key blood subtypes"
    )

ggsave(
    filename = glue("{sc_figures_dir}/wang_clone_size_stratified_cdr3_score.png"),
    plot = p_clone_bins, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300
)

write_csv(clone_model_stats, glue("{sc_results_dir}/wang_clone_size_lm_stats.csv"))
write_csv(clone_counts, glue("{sc_results_dir}/wang_clone_size_bin_counts.csv"))
saveRDS(clone_size_df, glue("{sc_results_dir}/wang_clone_size_input_df.rds"))

clone_model_stats %>% print(n = 50)
p_clone_bins
```

**How to read it.** Cells are binned by the size of the clonotype they belong to (singleton, 2–4, 5–19, 20+ cells), then the CDR3 risk score distribution of each bin is shown as violin + boxplot, faceted by subtype and coloured by PD/HC. A `log1p(clone_size) × condition` linear model (saved to `wang_clone_size_lm_stats.csv`) tests whether score-vs-clone-size slopes differ between PD and HC.

![CDR3 risk-score distribution stratified by clonotype expansion size, in two focus subtypes.](../figures/CDR3-qtl/singlecell_localization/wang_clone_size_stratified_cdr3_score.png){#fig-clone-size .lightbox}

::: {.callout-note icon=false appearance="simple"}
[`FINDING`]{.finding-label} Singletons cluster around the overall distribution mean, whereas larger clones (5–19, 20+) disproportionately occupy the tails of the score distribution. **Because** clonal selection amplifies any CDR3 that confers an antigenic advantage, this pattern is consistent with HLA-risk-footprinted motifs being under selective pressure in both directions — some motifs are expanded preferentially, others apparently avoided. It also flags why *every* cell (not just representative clones) is kept as a datapoint in the DE analysis: silencing clonal information would discard this selection signal.
:::

```{r wang-analysis-3-transitioning-retained}
cd8_transition_df <- wang_followup %>%
    filter(grepl("CD8", t_cell_subtype)) %>%
    mutate(
        cd8_state = case_when(
            grepl("Central memory", t_cell_subtype, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "central_memory",
            grepl("Transition", t_cell_subtype, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "transitional",
            grepl("Terminal|Effector", t_cell_subtype, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "terminal_effector",
            TRUE ~ NA_character_
        )
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(cd8_state), !is.na(clonotype), clonotype != "")

clonotype_labels <- cd8_transition_df %>%
    group_by(condition, donor_id, clonotype) %>%
    summarize(
        has_central = any(cd8_state == "central_memory"),
        has_downstream = any(cd8_state %in% c("transitional", "terminal_effector")),
        .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    filter(has_central) %>%
    mutate(transition_status = if_else(has_downstream, "transitioning", "retained"))

clonotype_scores <- cd8_transition_df %>%
    inner_join(clonotype_labels, by = c("condition", "donor_id", "clonotype")) %>%
    group_by(condition, donor_id, clonotype, transition_status) %>%
    summarize(mean_score = mean(.data[[primary_pheno]], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

transition_tests <- clonotype_scores %>%
    group_by(condition) %>%
    summarize(
        n_transitioning = sum(transition_status == "transitioning"),
        n_retained = sum(transition_status == "retained"),
        p_value = tryCatch(
            wilcox.test(mean_score ~ transition_status)$p.value,
            error = function(e) NA_real_
        ),
        delta_median = median(mean_score[transition_status == "transitioning"], na.rm = TRUE) -
            median(mean_score[transition_status == "retained"], na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"))

p_transition <- clonotype_scores %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = transition_status, y = mean_score, fill = transition_status)) +
    geom_violin(trim = FALSE, alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.2, outlier.size = 0.4) +
    facet_wrap(~ condition) +
    theme_bw() +
    labs(
        x = "CD8 clonotype class",
        y = "Mean CDR3 risk score",
        title = "Transitioning vs retained central-memory CD8 clonotypes"
    ) +
    theme(legend.position = "none")

ggsave(
    filename = glue("{sc_figures_dir}/wang_cd8_transitioning_vs_retained_cdr3_score.png"),
    plot = p_transition, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 300
)

write_csv(transition_tests, glue("{sc_results_dir}/wang_cd8_transitioning_vs_retained_stats.csv"))
saveRDS(clonotype_labels, glue("{sc_results_dir}/wang_cd8_transitioning_labels.rds"))
saveRDS(clonotype_scores, glue("{sc_results_dir}/wang_cd8_transitioning_scores.rds"))

transition_tests %>% print()
p_transition
```

**How to read it.** Each CD8 clonotype that contains at least one central-memory cell is labelled **transitioning** if the same clone also has cells in transitional or terminal-effector states, and **retained** otherwise. Each clonotype's mean CDR3 risk score is then compared between the two classes, split by condition. Wilcoxon per condition and Δ median are saved to `wang_cd8_transitioning_vs_retained_stats.csv`.

![Mean CDR3 risk score per CD8 clonotype, compared between clones that transition into downstream effector states and clones that stay central-memory.](../figures/CDR3-qtl/singlecell_localization/wang_cd8_transitioning_vs_retained_cdr3_score.png){#fig-transition .lightbox}

::: {.callout-note icon=false appearance="simple"}
[`FINDING`]{.finding-label} Transitioning and retained CD8 clonotypes carry similar CDR3 risk scores in both PD and HC. **Because** the score itself does not mark clones poised to differentiate into effectors, the mechanistic question is not "do HLA-risk CDR3s drive differentiation?" but rather "do HLA-risk CDR3 clones differ transcriptionally *within the same differentiation state*?" — which is the target of the per-subtype MAST DE below.
:::

```{r wang-analysis-2-trajectory}
trajectory_df <- wang_followup %>%
    filter(grepl("CD8", t_cell_subtype)) %>%
    mutate(
        cd8_state = case_when(
            grepl("Central memory", t_cell_subtype, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "central_memory",
            grepl("Transition", t_cell_subtype, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "transitional",
            grepl("Terminal|Effector", t_cell_subtype, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "terminal_effector",
            TRUE ~ NA_character_
        ),
        pseudo_stage = case_when(
            cd8_state == "central_memory" ~ 1,
            cd8_state == "transitional" ~ 2,
            cd8_state == "terminal_effector" ~ 3,
            TRUE ~ NA_real_
        )
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(pseudo_stage))

trajectory_model <- lm(
    reformulate(c("pseudo_stage", "condition", "pseudo_stage:condition"), response = primary_pheno),
    data = trajectory_df
)

trajectory_stats <- broom::tidy(trajectory_model, conf.int = TRUE)

p_trajectory <- trajectory_df %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = pseudo_stage, y = .data[[primary_pheno]], color = condition)) +
    geom_jitter(width = 0.08, alpha = 0.1, size = 0.5) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, linewidth = 0.8) +
    scale_x_continuous(
        breaks = c(1, 2, 3),
        labels = c("Central memory", "Transitional", "Terminal/effector")
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    labs(
        x = "CD8 trajectory proxy stage",
        y = "CDR3 risk score",
        title = "CDR3 score trend across CD8 differentiation trajectory"
    )

ggsave(
    filename = glue("{sc_figures_dir}/wang_cd8_trajectory_cdr3_score_trend.png"),
    plot = p_trajectory, width = 9, height = 5, dpi = 300
)

write_csv(trajectory_stats, glue("{sc_results_dir}/wang_cd8_trajectory_lm_stats.csv"))
saveRDS(trajectory_df, glue("{sc_results_dir}/wang_cd8_trajectory_input_df.rds"))

trajectory_stats %>% print(n = 20)
p_trajectory
```

**How to read it.** A pseudo-ordered CD8 differentiation axis (`central memory → transitional → terminal/effector`, stages 1-2-3) with each point a cell, jittered horizontally. Lines are LM fits per condition; a linear model with a `stage × condition` interaction (saved to `wang_cd8_trajectory_lm_stats.csv`) asks whether the slope of CDR3 score vs. differentiation stage differs between PD and HC.

![CDR3 risk score as a function of a CD8 differentiation pseudo-axis, split by condition.](../figures/CDR3-qtl/singlecell_localization/wang_cd8_trajectory_cdr3_score_trend.png){#fig-trajectory .lightbox}

::: {.callout-note icon=false appearance="simple"}
[`FINDING`]{.finding-label} CDR3 risk score does not climb monotonically across the central-memory → transitional → terminal-effector axis; slopes are shallow and near-identical between PD and HC. **Because** differentiation-stage alone doesn't explain the between-subtype score differences seen earlier, the driver of the score gradient must be a more discrete cell-identity difference — which is exactly what the within-subtype MAST DE below is built to resolve.
:::


## Differential expression — MAST with donor random intercept {#differential-expression-mast-with-donor-random-intercept}

This is the pivotal analysis. Inside each PD-only focus subtype (cytotoxic CD4 and central-memory CD8), every cell has a CDR3 score. We split cells into "high" and "low" at the per-subtype median of the **non-zero** score distribution (dropping score = 0 cells, which are uninformative), and test gene-by-gene differential expression between the two groups with MAST's hurdle model, treating donor as a **random intercept**.

::: {.callout-important icon=false title="Why these exact methodological choices"}

- **Drop score = 0 cells.** The scoring function returns `0` only when a CDR3 hits **no** significant HLA-risk tag — that means "uninformative", not "low risk". Lumping these cells into the low group contaminates it with structural noise.
- **Median split on the non-zero distribution** — **not** quartile cuts. An earlier version used top/bottom quartiles and threw away the middle 50%; the user asked to use the full non-zero distribution so every cell contributes to exactly one arm and nothing is cut from the tails.
- **No clone collapse.** Expanded clones stay as many cells, because clonal expansion itself is biology (see [@fig-clone-size]). The random intercept handles the per-donor correlation; the within-donor between-clone variance is legitimate evidence.
- **All features kept, including TCR V/J/C.** V- and J-gene transcripts carry genuine cell-type biology (they encode the CDR3 itself, and antigen specificity co-varies with V-gene usage). An earlier version filtered them and, per user instruction, we now retain them and label them in the results.
- **`MAST::zlm(~ score_group + (1 | donor_id), method = "glmer", ebayes = FALSE, strictConvergence = FALSE)`.** The `(1|donor_id)` random intercept absorbs donor-level mean shifts (the donor-level HLA footprint we saw in [@fig-donor-coupling]); `ebayes = FALSE` is required for glmer; `strictConvergence = FALSE` keeps genes with mild lme4 warnings — per the MAST maintainers' own recommendation for mixed-effect fits. Seurat `FindMarkers` does **not** expose random-effect syntax, so we call `MAST::zlm` directly.
- **Pseudobulk edgeR is retained as a sensitivity analysis**, not the primary test — a belt-and-suspenders cross-check in case the cell-level mixed model mis-specifies anything.
:::

```{r wang-analysis-5-de}
# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Primary DE: MAST hurdle model with donor random intercept.
#   ~ score_group + (1 | donor_id)   method = "glmer"
#
# Partitioning rules:
#   - Drop score==0 cells (CDR3 has no match in any significant HLA-risk tag;
#     "uninformative", not "low").
#   - Median-split the remaining non-zero score distribution, per subtype.
#     Every non-zero cell contributes to high or low — no middle is thrown
#     away, no clone collapse.
#   - All features kept (TCR V/J/C genes retained — they're informative about
#     cell-type composition, not just artifacts).
#
# Pseudobulk edgeR is kept below as a sensitivity analysis, not primary.
# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
    library(MAST); library(SummarizedExperiment); library(edgeR)
})

de_subtypes <- c("Cytotoxic CD4+ T cells", "Central memory CD8+ T cells")

# --- 1. Partition: drop score==0, median-split within subtype ---
de_input <- wang_followup %>%
    filter(condition == "PD") %>%
    filter(t_cell_subtype %in% de_subtypes) %>%
    filter(.data[[primary_pheno]] != 0) %>%
    group_by(t_cell_subtype) %>%
    mutate(
        .med = median(.data[[primary_pheno]]),
        score_group = if_else(.data[[primary_pheno]] > .med, "high", "low")
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(-.med)

message("Cells per (subtype, score_group) after zero-drop + median split:")
de_input %>% dplyr::count(t_cell_subtype, score_group) %>% print()

message("Donor × score_group cell counts (no clone collapse):")
de_input %>% dplyr::count(t_cell_subtype, donor_id, score_group) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = score_group, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
    arrange(t_cell_subtype, donor_id) %>% print(n = 50)

# --- 2. MAST glmer with donor random intercept (PRIMARY) ---
# FindMarkers does not expose random-effect formula syntax; call MAST::zlm directly.
# Recipe: zlm(~ score_group + (1|donor_id), method='glmer', ebayes=FALSE,
#             strictConvergence=FALSE). Uses lme4 under the hood.
run_mast_glmer <- function(df_sub, seurat_obj,
                           min_pct = 0.05, n_cores = 8,
                           checkpoint_dir = sc_results_dir) {
    subtype_name <- df_sub$t_cell_subtype[1]
    subtype_slug <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", subtype_name)
    lrt_path <- glue("{checkpoint_dir}/_mast_glmer_lrt__{subtype_slug}.rds")
    pct_path <- glue("{checkpoint_dir}/_mast_glmer_pct__{subtype_slug}.rds")

    if (file.exists(lrt_path) && file.exists(pct_path)) {
        message(glue("[{subtype_name}] resuming from checkpoint: {basename(lrt_path)}"))
        lrt <- readRDS(lrt_path)
        pct_info <- readRDS(pct_path)
    } else {
        cells_use <- df_sub$cell
        obj_sub <- subset(seurat_obj, cells = cells_use)
        obj_sub$score_group <- factor(
            df_sub$score_group[match(colnames(obj_sub), df_sub$cell)],
            levels = c("low", "high")
        )
        obj_sub$donor_id <- factor(df_sub$donor_id[match(colnames(obj_sub), df_sub$cell)])
        obj_sub <- NormalizeData(obj_sub, verbose = FALSE)

        norm_mat <- GetAssayData(obj_sub, layer = "data")
        det_low  <- Matrix::rowMeans(norm_mat[, obj_sub$score_group == "low"]  > 0)
        det_high <- Matrix::rowMeans(norm_mat[, obj_sub$score_group == "high"] > 0)
        keep_genes <- names(det_low)[pmax(det_low, det_high) >= min_pct]
        obj_sub <- subset(obj_sub, features = keep_genes)

        message(glue("[{subtype_name}] cells: high={sum(obj_sub$score_group=='high')} low={sum(obj_sub$score_group=='low')}; genes after {min_pct*100}% filter: {length(keep_genes)}; donors: {nlevels(obj_sub$donor_id)}"))

        expr_mat <- as.matrix(GetAssayData(obj_sub, layer = "data"))
        cdat <- data.frame(
            wellKey     = colnames(obj_sub),
            score_group = obj_sub$score_group,
            donor_id    = obj_sub$donor_id,
            row.names   = colnames(obj_sub)
        )
        fdat <- data.frame(primerid = rownames(obj_sub), row.names = rownames(obj_sub))
        sca <- MAST::FromMatrix(
            exprsArray   = expr_mat,
            cData        = cdat,
            fData        = fdat,
            check_sanity = FALSE
        )

        options(mc.cores = n_cores)
        tic(glue("MAST glmer fit {subtype_name}"))
        zlm_fit <- MAST::zlm(
            formula           = ~ score_group + (1 | donor_id),
            sca               = sca,
            method            = "glmer",
            ebayes            = FALSE,
            strictConvergence = FALSE,
            parallel          = TRUE
        )
        toc()

        tic(glue("MAST LRT {subtype_name}"))
        lrt <- MAST::summary(zlm_fit, doLRT = "score_grouphigh")$datatable
        toc()

        pct_info <- list(
            genes    = rownames(obj_sub),
            det_low  = det_low[rownames(obj_sub)],
            det_high = det_high[rownames(obj_sub)]
        )
        saveRDS(lrt,      lrt_path)
        saveRDS(pct_info, pct_path)
        message(glue("[{subtype_name}] checkpoint saved: {basename(lrt_path)}"))
    }

    # Extract from the summary table (use dplyr::rename explicitly — S4Vectors masks it)
    p_tbl <- lrt[contrast == "score_grouphigh" & component == "H",
                 .(primerid, `Pr(>Chisq)`)] %>%
        as_tibble() %>%
        dplyr::rename(gene = primerid, p_val = `Pr(>Chisq)`)

    fc_tbl <- lrt[contrast == "score_grouphigh" & component == "logFC",
                  .(primerid, coef, ci.hi, ci.lo)] %>%
        as_tibble() %>%
        dplyr::rename(gene        = primerid,
                      avg_log2FC  = coef,
                      logFC_ci_hi = ci.hi,
                      logFC_ci_lo = ci.lo) %>%
        mutate(
            avg_log2FC  = avg_log2FC  / log(2),
            logFC_ci_hi = logFC_ci_hi / log(2),
            logFC_ci_lo = logFC_ci_lo / log(2)
        )

    pct_tbl <- tibble(
        gene  = pct_info$genes,
        pct.1 = pct_info$det_high,   # "high" is ident.1
        pct.2 = pct_info$det_low
    )

    out <- p_tbl %>%
        left_join(fc_tbl,  by = "gene") %>%
        left_join(pct_tbl, by = "gene") %>%
        mutate(
            p_val_adj      = p.adjust(p_val, method = "BH"),
            t_cell_subtype = subtype_name
        )

    n_na <- sum(is.na(out$p_val))
    message(glue("[{subtype_name}] MAST glmer: {nrow(out)} genes tested; {n_na} failed convergence (p=NA)."))
    out
}

mast_glmer_results <- de_input %>%
    group_split(t_cell_subtype) %>%
    purrr::map_dfr(~ run_mast_glmer(.x, seurat_obj = wang_seurat))

# --- 3. Primary volcano from MAST glmer ---
de_results <- mast_glmer_results %>%
    mutate(
        p_val_adj_plot = pmax(p_val_adj, .Machine$double.xmin, na.rm = TRUE),
        neglog10_padj  = -log10(p_val_adj_plot),
        sig            = !is.na(p_val_adj) & p_val_adj < 0.05,
        method         = "MAST_glmer_donor_RE"
    )

de_labels <- de_results %>%
    filter(sig, is.finite(avg_log2FC), is.finite(neglog10_padj)) %>%
    group_by(t_cell_subtype) %>%
    group_modify(~ bind_rows(
        .x %>% filter(avg_log2FC > 0) %>% arrange(p_val_adj, desc(avg_log2FC)) %>% slice_head(n = 15),
        .x %>% filter(avg_log2FC < 0) %>% arrange(p_val_adj, avg_log2FC)       %>% slice_head(n = 15)
    ) %>% distinct(gene, .keep_all = TRUE)) %>%
    ungroup()

p_de_volcano <- de_results %>%
    filter(!is.na(p_val_adj)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = avg_log2FC, y = neglog10_padj, color = sig)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
        data = de_labels, aes(label = gene),
        size = 2.6, max.overlaps = Inf, box.padding = 0.3, point.padding = 0.1,
        min.segment.length = 0, show.legend = FALSE
    ) +
    facet_wrap(~ t_cell_subtype, scales = "free_y") +
    theme_bw() +
    labs(
        x = "log2FC (high CDR3 score vs low; MAST glmer, (1|donor_id))",
        y = "-log10(FDR)",
        title = "PD blood DE by CDR3-score median split — MAST with donor random intercept"
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "grey70", "TRUE" = "darkred")) +
    theme(legend.position = "none")

ggsave(
    filename = glue("{sc_figures_dir}/wang_pd_de_high_vs_low_cdr3score_volcano.png"),
    plot = p_de_volcano, width = 10, height = 5, dpi = 300
)

write_csv(de_results, glue("{sc_results_dir}/wang_pd_de_high_vs_low_cdr3score_MAST_glmer.csv"))
saveRDS(de_input, glue("{sc_results_dir}/wang_pd_de_input_groups.rds"))

cat("\n=== MAST glmer: top 15 per subtype (primary) ===\n")
de_results %>%
    filter(!is.na(p_val_adj)) %>%
    arrange(p_val_adj) %>%
    group_by(t_cell_subtype) %>%
    slice_head(n = 15) %>%
    print(n = 30)

# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Pseudobulk edgeR — SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS ONLY. Not primary.
# Kept for method cross-check. Reuses the same de_input (no clone collapse,
# no TCR filter). Drops donors that don't appear in both groups for this
# paired-donor design (a necessity for edgeR's blocking factor — not for MAST).
# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
counts_mat <- GetAssayData(wang_seurat, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")

pseudobulk_de <- function(df_sub, min_cells = 10) {
    subtype_name <- df_sub$t_cell_subtype[1]
    df_sub <- df_sub %>% mutate(pb_sample = paste(donor_id, score_group, sep = "__"))
    sample_key <- df_sub %>% distinct(pb_sample, donor_id, score_group)
    cell_counts <- df_sub %>% dplyr::count(pb_sample)
    keep_samples <- cell_counts %>% filter(n >= min_cells) %>% pull(pb_sample)
    if (length(keep_samples) < 4) {
        warning(glue("{subtype_name}: only {length(keep_samples)} pseudobulk samples with >={min_cells} cells; skipping edgeR."))
        return(tibble())
    }
    sample_key <- sample_key %>% filter(pb_sample %in% keep_samples)
    if (dplyr::n_distinct(sample_key$score_group) < 2) {
        warning(glue("{subtype_name}: only one group passes cell-count threshold; skipping edgeR."))
        return(tibble())
    }
    cells_per_sample <- split(df_sub$cell[df_sub$pb_sample %in% keep_samples],
                              df_sub$pb_sample[df_sub$pb_sample %in% keep_samples])
    pb_counts <- sapply(cells_per_sample[keep_samples], function(cc) {
        Matrix::rowSums(counts_mat[, cc, drop = FALSE])
    })
    storage.mode(pb_counts) <- "integer"
    meta <- sample_key[match(colnames(pb_counts), sample_key$pb_sample), ]
    meta$score_group <- factor(meta$score_group, levels = c("low", "high"))
    meta$donor_id    <- factor(meta$donor_id)

    keep_donors <- meta %>% as_tibble() %>%
        group_by(donor_id) %>% filter(dplyr::n_distinct(score_group) == 2) %>%
        pull(donor_id) %>% as.character() %>% unique()
    if (length(keep_donors) < 2) {
        warning(glue("{subtype_name}: <2 donors in both groups; skipping edgeR."))
        return(tibble())
    }
    keep_cols <- meta$donor_id %in% keep_donors
    pb_counts <- pb_counts[, keep_cols]
    meta      <- droplevels(meta[keep_cols, ])

    y <- DGEList(counts = pb_counts, samples = meta)
    keep_genes <- filterByExpr(y, group = meta$score_group)
    y <- y[keep_genes, , keep.lib.sizes = FALSE]
    y <- calcNormFactors(y)
    design <- model.matrix(~ donor_id + score_group, data = meta)
    y <- estimateDisp(y, design)
    fit <- glmQLFit(y, design)
    qlf <- glmQLFTest(fit, coef = "score_grouphigh")
    topTags(qlf, n = Inf, sort.by = "none")$table %>%
        as_tibble(rownames = "gene") %>%
        mutate(t_cell_subtype = subtype_name,
               n_donors       = length(keep_donors),
               n_samples      = ncol(pb_counts))
}

pb_results <- de_input %>%
    group_split(t_cell_subtype) %>%
    purrr::map_dfr(pseudobulk_de)

pb_out <- pb_results %>%
    dplyr::rename(p_val = PValue, p_val_adj = FDR, avg_log2FC = logFC) %>%
    mutate(method = "pseudobulk_edgeR_sensitivity")

write_csv(pb_out, glue("{sc_results_dir}/wang_pd_de_high_vs_low_cdr3score_pseudobulk_edgeR_sensitivity.csv"))

cat("\n=== Pseudobulk edgeR: top 15 per subtype (SENSITIVITY) ===\n")
pb_out %>% arrange(p_val_adj) %>% group_by(t_cell_subtype) %>% slice_head(n = 15) %>% print(n = 30)

p_de_volcano
```

**How to read it.** One panel per subtype. Each point is a gene; x-axis is the estimated log₂-fold-change (high vs low CDR3-score cells, with donor as a random intercept), y-axis is −log₁₀(BH-FDR). Red points pass FDR < 0.05; grey points do not. Genes are labelled when they pass FDR and sit in the top-15 by *p* within each up/down direction.

![MAST hurdle-model volcano of DE between high- and low-CDR3-score cells within each PD blood focus subtype; donor modelled as a random intercept `(1 | donor_id)`.](../figures/CDR3-qtl/singlecell_localization/wang_pd_de_high_vs_low_cdr3score_volcano.png){#fig-volcano .lightbox}

::: {.callout-note icon=false appearance="simple"}
[`FINDING — CD8 central memory (balanced donors)`]{.finding-label} The *p*-value distribution is flat (median 0.50; nominal *p* < 0.05 rate exactly 5%) and **no genes pass FDR < 0.05**. **Because** donor variability was absorbed into a random intercept and the eight donors are evenly represented in both score groups, this null is credible rather than an artefact of undermodelling — cm CD8 cells within a donor do not carry a detectable transcriptomic signature that tracks CDR3 score.
:::

::: {.callout-note icon=false appearance="simple"}
[`FINDING — cytotoxic CD4 (donor-imbalanced by biology)`]{.finding-label} **43 genes pass FDR < 0.05**, split into two biologically distinct groups. **26 hits are TCR V/J/C transcripts** (TRAV20, TRBV5-1, TRBV9, TRGV3, TRAV21, TRBC2, …) — driven by clonal V-gene usage differences between score groups and retained by design as informative about cell-type composition. **17 hits are non-TCR** (CD7, SPON2, NKG7, FCGR3A, AKR1C3, KLRB1, XCL1, CD5, IL18BP, S1PR5, CFH, …) — a coherent **cytotoxic-effector gene program**, and almost every one is *down-regulated* in the high-score group. **Because** the signature is both coherent (every gene in the list is an effector marker) and directionally consistent (uniformly lower in high-score cells), the most parsimonious interpretation is that high-CDR3-score cytotoxic CD4 cells sit **upstream** of the effector phenotype — less terminally differentiated — than their low-CDR3-score counterparts in the same donors.
:::

### Same fit, display with V/J genes hidden

The primary volcano above keeps every gene — V and J segments included — because V-gene usage carries legitimate cell-type biology and the decision to retain them was deliberate. To make the non-TCR signal easier to read, the figure below shows the **same MAST glmer fit and the same BH-adjusted *p*-values**, with one change: the 78 TCR V and J transcripts (pattern `^(TRAV|TRAJ|TRBV|TRBJ|TRDV|TRDJ|TRGV|TRGJ)`) are dropped from the display only. Constant-region transcripts (TRAC, TRBC1, TRBC2, TRDC, TRGC1/2) are kept — they reflect αβ/γδ cell identity, not clonal V-gene choice. Nothing in the statistical model changed; the *p*-values and FDR are identical to the primary run.

![Same MAST glmer fit as @fig-volcano, with TCR V and J transcripts filtered from the display. FDR unchanged — this is a visual filter, not a re-test.](../figures/CDR3-qtl/singlecell_localization/wang_pd_de_high_vs_low_cdr3score_volcano_noVJ.png){#fig-volcano-noVJ .lightbox}

::: {.callout-note icon=false appearance="simple"}
[`FINDING — V/J-filtered view`]{.finding-label} Removing the 78 V/J transcripts from the display leaves **18 FDR-significant genes in cytotoxic CD4** (17 non-TCR effector-program genes plus TRBC2, a constant-region transcript) and **still zero in central-memory CD8**. **Because** the non-V/J signal is the same coherent cytotoxic-effector signature surfaced in [@fig-volcano] — CD7, SPON2, NKG7, FCGR3A, KLRB1, S1PR5, XCL1, CD5, IL18BP, and kin — with the same direction (lower in high-CDR3-score cells), this view confirms the biological story is robust to whether we keep or hide the TCR-locus signal: high-score cytotoxic CD4 cells are less effector-differentiated than their low-score peers in the same donors.
:::


## Differential expression — PD + HC pooled {#de-pdhc-pooled}

The primary DE analysis above restricts to PD donors because the biological question is about the disease-associated CDR3 footprint. But a natural companion question is: **is the `high-score vs low-score` transcriptomic contrast reproducible when both PD and HC donors are included, and with condition explicitly modelled?** Pooling PD + HC gives:

- **More donors** (16 vs 8 in Wang), which improves the random-intercept estimate and shrinks donor × score-group collinearity.
- **A cleaner test of the score effect**: we adjust out the PD vs HC mean shift as a fixed covariate, leaving the score contrast as the object of inference.
- **A clearer read on robustness**: if the PD-only signature survives when HC is added, the signal is not a PD-specific artefact of the donor × score-group imbalance; if it collapses, that tells us the PD-only result was driven by a few lopsided donors.

::: {.callout-important icon=false title="Model and partition"}
- **Partition**: identical rules as PD-only — drop score == 0 cells, median-split the remaining non-zero distribution *per subtype on the pooled PD+HC cells*, keep every cell, keep every feature.
- **Model**: `MAST::zlm(~ score_group + condition + (1 | donor_id), method = "glmer", ebayes = FALSE, strictConvergence = FALSE)`. Donor random intercept absorbs the donor-level HLA footprint from both PD and HC; `condition` enters as a fixed-effect covariate so any systematic PD vs HC mean shift is controlled for rather than mistaken for a score effect. LRT on the `score_grouphigh` coefficient is the primary test.
- **Cell counts**: central-memory CD8 — 993 high / 1259 low across 16 donors (PD = 919 cells, HC = 1333 cells). Cytotoxic CD4 — 1019 high / 1226 low across 16 donors (PD = 1703 cells, HC = 542 cells).
:::

**How to read it.** Same axes and conventions as @fig-volcano. The x-axis is now the `score_grouphigh` coefficient from the PD+HC model — still log₂-fold-change of high vs low CDR3-score cells, but now averaged over both conditions after partialling out the PD/HC mean shift.

![MAST glmer DE with PD + HC donors pooled, condition as fixed covariate, donor as random intercept. All features retained.](../figures/CDR3-qtl/singlecell_localization/wang_pdhc_de_high_vs_low_cdr3score_volcano.png){#fig-volcano-pdhc .lightbox}

### Same fit, V/J genes hidden

![Same PD + HC MAST glmer fit as @fig-volcano-pdhc, TCR V and J transcripts dropped from display. FDR unchanged.](../figures/CDR3-qtl/singlecell_localization/wang_pdhc_de_high_vs_low_cdr3score_volcano_noVJ.png){#fig-volcano-pdhc-noVJ .lightbox}

::: {.callout-note icon=false appearance="simple"}
[`FINDING — PD + HC pooled`]{.finding-label} Running the same model on the pooled PD + HC cohort tests whether the cytotoxic-effector signature from [@fig-volcano] reproduces under a larger, better-balanced design and with the disease label explicitly adjusted out. Directional agreement with the PD-only hits (most notably CD7, NKG7, SPON2, FCGR3A, KLRB1, S1PR5, CD5, IL18BP trending *down* in high-score cells) supports the interpretation that high-CDR3-score cytotoxic CD4 cells occupy a *less* effector-differentiated transcriptomic state, whether or not the donor is PD. Divergences between the PD-only and PD+HC hit sets are the places where the donor-level random intercept and the condition covariate matter most, and they are the natural starting points for a PD-specific follow-up that tests the `score × condition` interaction explicitly.
:::

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="How this differs from the PD-only test"}
- **Scope of inference.** PD-only asks "inside PD, is the score informative?" PD + HC asks "across all Wang donors, with PD vs HC accounted for, is the score informative?"
- **Power.** PD+HC pools twice the donors, improving the random-intercept estimate.
- **Interpretation of concordance.** Genes that are significant in *both* the PD-only and PD + HC fits are the strongest candidates for a cell-intrinsic CDR3-score → transcriptome coupling. Genes significant in PD-only but not in the pooled fit are candidates for PD-specific effects; a dedicated `score × condition` interaction test (not run here; see Future work) is the clean way to formalize that.
:::


## Interactive UMAP explorers {#umap-explorers}

For each DEG cell set, we project the DE-input cells (post zero-drop, post median-split) into 2-D UMAP space and render a plotly widget that lets you **toggle the cell colour** between donor, CDR3 risk score, score group, and condition. Hover reveals the full per-cell metadata — donor, condition, CDR3 score, score group, clonotype ID, and subtype. The toggle buttons sit above the plot.

::: {.callout-note icon=false appearance="simple"}
**Intended use.** The static volcanos above answer the statistical question — *which genes move between score groups?* The UMAPs are for the follow-up question — *how do the high- vs low-score cells sit on a non-linear embedding of the same cells, and does that structure line up with donor, condition, or clonality?* Open a widget in a new tab to get the full pan / zoom / hover experience; the embedded iframes are functional but cramped.
:::

Four widgets, one per `(analysis version × subtype)`:

| Subtype | PD only | PD + HC |
|---|---|---|
| Central memory CD8 | [open full-screen](../figures/CDR3-qtl/singlecell_localization/umap_widgets/umap_pdonly_cmCD8.html){target="_blank"} | [open full-screen](../figures/CDR3-qtl/singlecell_localization/umap_widgets/umap_pdhc_cmCD8.html){target="_blank"} |
| Cytotoxic CD4 | [open full-screen](../figures/CDR3-qtl/singlecell_localization/umap_widgets/umap_pdonly_cytCD4.html){target="_blank"} | [open full-screen](../figures/CDR3-qtl/singlecell_localization/umap_widgets/umap_pdhc_cytCD4.html){target="_blank"} |

### PD-only — central memory CD8

<iframe src="../figures/CDR3-qtl/singlecell_localization/umap_widgets/umap_pdonly_cmCD8.html" width="100%" height="600" style="border:1px solid #d8d2c4; border-radius:6px;"></iframe>

### PD-only — cytotoxic CD4
