### PD + HC — central memory CD8

<iframe src="../figures/CDR3-qtl/singlecell_localization/umap_widgets/umap_pdhc_cmCD8.html" width="100%" height="600" style="border:1px solid #d8d2c4; border-radius:6px;"></iframe>

### PD + HC — cytotoxic CD4

<iframe src="../figures/CDR3-qtl/singlecell_localization/umap_widgets/umap_pdhc_cytCD4.html" width="100%" height="600" style="border:1px solid #d8d2c4; border-radius:6px;"></iframe>

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="What to look for"}
- **Colour by donor.** Tight per-donor clusters would signal that donor-level structure dominates the embedding — expected given the donor-level HLA footprint from [@fig-donor-coupling]. Diffuse, overlapping donors imply shared transcriptomic axes.
- **Colour by CDR3 risk score.** Smooth gradients along one UMAP axis implicate the score as aligned with a continuous transcriptomic state; speckled distributions implicate it as donor-driven or clonal.
- **Colour by score group.** The median split is what the DEG test uses. If high and low cells segregate visibly in UMAP, the DEG signal sits on a major cell-state axis rather than a minor perturbation.
- **Colour by condition.** In the PD + HC widgets, a PD vs HC visual split suggests the condition covariate in the MAST model is doing real work — it's partialling out a structural difference, not nothing.
:::

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Section takeaways — Wang mechanistic follow-ups"}

- **Donor coupling ([@fig-donor-coupling]):** the score is a donor-level property that projects onto multiple compartments — a textbook case for a random-intercept model.
- **Clonal expansion ([@fig-clone-size]):** larger clones carry more extreme scores in both directions, indicating selective pressure on HLA-footprinted motifs that we do not want to average out with clone collapsing.
- **CD8 trajectory ([@fig-trajectory]) and transitioning vs retained ([@fig-transition]):** the score does not rise monotonically with CD8 differentiation; trajectory-level variables are not the driver.
- **MAST glmer DE ([@fig-volcano]):** central-memory CD8 is transcriptomically null given the donor random intercept; cytotoxic CD4 carries a real, coherent cytotoxic-effector signature that is **lower** in high-score cells.
:::

::: {.callout-important icon=false title="Audit trail — how the DE analysis evolved"}
- The initial implementation used quartile cuts on all cells, fixed-effect `latent.vars = "donor_id"`, and reported 18 genes at FDR < 0.05 in central-memory CD8. **17 of those 18 hits were TCR V/J/C genes** driven by the circular association of CDR3 motif with V-gene identity; the one non-TCR hit (GNLY) was a weak outlier. That result was an artefact.
- In cytotoxic CD4, donor × group collinearity was severe (donor P8 contributed 219 "high" cells and 3 "low" cells; other donors were similarly lopsided). A fixed-effect donor covariate could not rescue this; 0 genes passed FDR.
- The partition was rebuilt to drop uninformative score = 0 cells and median-split the non-zero distribution — using the *full* distribution, not truncating the tails. Clones are kept uncollapsed. TCR V/J/C genes are kept, flagged, and interpreted explicitly. Donor is now a random intercept, not a fixed-effect covariate — the only modification that statistically absorbs the donor-level HLA footprint while leaving the within-donor signal estimable.
- Pseudobulk edgeR is retained as a sensitivity analysis below. RDS checkpoints (`_mast_glmer_{lrt,pct}__<subtype>.rds`) are written inside the helper, so a downstream crash does not force a second 30-minute `glmer` fit.
:::


# Conclusions {#conclusions}

## What the analysis shows

The CDR3-QTL HLA-risk score, originally a donor-level readout, resolves cleanly at single-cell resolution across three independent PD scRNA-seq + TCR-seq datasets.

- **Between subtypes** ([@fig-subtype-enrichment], [@fig-heatmap]). High-score CDR3-β motifs concentrate in antigen-experienced effector / cytotoxic compartments — cytotoxic CD4, central-memory CD8, effector CD8, TEMRA — and are depleted from naïve and regulatory subsets. γδ T cells form a distinct compartment ([@fig-gd-markers]) with their own score profile. This pattern is stable across tissues.
- **Between donors** ([@fig-donor-coupling]). A donor's mean CDR3 score in one antigen-experienced compartment predicts the same donor's score in a second compartment (cm CD8 ↔ cytotoxic CD4), consistent with the score reflecting the donor's HLA-footprint rather than a compartment-specific signal.
- **Between PD and HC** ([@fig-pd-hc-shift]). The strongest condition-level shifts are in cytotoxic CD4 and central-memory CD8 in blood; CSF shifts are present but attenuated by cell counts.
- **Within donor, within subtype** ([@fig-volcano]). After dropping uninformative score = 0 cells, splitting the non-zero distribution at the median, retaining every cell and every feature, and absorbing donor variability into a random intercept:
  - **Central-memory CD8**: no gene-expression signature distinguishes high- from low-CDR3-score cells. The *p*-value distribution is flat (median 0.50, nominal *p* < 0.05 rate exactly 5%).
  - **Cytotoxic CD4**: 43 FDR-significant genes. 26 are TCR V/J/C transcripts (clonal V-gene usage skew between score groups) and 17 are non-TCR — **CD7, SPON2, NKG7, FCGR3A, KLRB1, S1PR5, XCL1, CD5, IL18BP, AKR1C3, CFH, …** — a coherent cytotoxic-effector program that is uniformly *lower* in the high-score group.
- **Pooling PD + HC with condition as a fixed covariate** ([@fig-volcano-pdhc], [@fig-volcano-pdhc-noVJ]). The same model, run on all 16 Wang donors (8 PD + 8 HC) with `condition` partialled out, tests whether the cytotoxic-CD4 signature is robust to the broader cohort. Directional agreement with the PD-only hits (the same effector-program genes trending down in high-score cells) supports a donor-independent, cell-intrinsic coupling between CDR3 risk score and effector-differentiation state in cytotoxic CD4.

## How we arrive at those claims

- **Subtype-level claims** come from one-vs-rest Wilcoxon on raw per-cell scores within each tissue ([@fig-subtype-enrichment]), per-subtype PD-vs-HC Wilcoxon ([@fig-pd-hc-shift]), and per-tissue Kruskal–Wallis for global tests. None of these depend on mixed-effect modelling; they describe the repertoire's geography.
- **Donor-level claims** come from per-donor mean scores followed by Pearson / Spearman correlation across donors within each condition ([@fig-donor-coupling]).
- **Within-donor within-subtype claims** come from the **MAST hurdle with random donor intercept** ([@fig-volcano]). Donor as a random intercept is the statistically conservative choice, because it absorbs exactly the donor-level mean shift that [@fig-donor-coupling] demonstrates is real. Fixed-effect donor covariates would over-fit in the presence of severe donor × group imbalance (P8: 219 high vs 3 low in CD4) and drown the signal in either null direction depending on which donors happened to tilt which way.
- **What we deliberately did *not* do.** We did not truncate the score distribution at extreme quantiles (middle cells contribute real information). We did not collapse clonotypes (clonal expansion is selection signal, [@fig-clone-size]). We did not filter TCR V/J/C genes (V-gene usage is legitimate cell-type biology); instead we flag them in the results and read them alongside the non-TCR hits.

## Implications

- The CDR3 risk-score is a **donor-level property** that sorts at the level of antigen-experienced compartments, not by broad CD4/CD8 class or by differentiation stage.
- Inside PD cytotoxic CD4 cells, **high-CDR3-score clones sit upstream of the fully effector phenotype**: they express *less* of the canonical cytotoxic program (NKG7, SPON2, FCGR3A, KLRB1, S1PR5) than their low-score counterparts from the same donors. This is the first direct transcriptomic correlate we have for the HLA-risk CDR3 footprint at single-cell resolution.
- Inside PD central-memory CD8 cells, **there is no such correlate** once donor variability is modelled properly. The earlier "18 significant genes" result was a TCR-circularity + fixed-donor artefact; its absence now is informative, not a regression.

## What remains open

- **Replication.** The cytotoxic-CD4 effector-axis signature needs a second, independent PD cohort. Moquin-Beaudry et al. 2025 is the natural replication dataset; the harmonize + score + DE pipeline is already wired to fold it in automatically once GEO is public.
- **Brain compartment.** Ma 2025 contributes 7,138 TRB CDR3s (535 T cells in PD SN) — enough to confirm the score distribution is not blood-identical, but insufficient for within-subtype within-donor DE. A larger brain cohort would be needed.
- **HLA mechanism.** If the cytotoxic-CD4 signature replicates, the next question ties it back to the origin of the score: do the donors who carry the strongest shift also carry the highest PD-risk-allele HLA dosage? That test re-connects the single-cell readout to the CDR3-QTL model it was derived from.
- **Atypical Parkinsonism.** Moquin-Beaudry 2025 includes 6 atypical Parkinsonism donors; when the data arrives, the same pipeline will tell us whether the signature is PD-specific or common to broader Parkinsonian syndromes.
- **PD-specific vs shared signal.** The PD + HC pooled fit above ([@fig-volcano-pdhc]) tests whether the score-vs-transcriptome contrast is robust to the larger cohort. A clean follow-up is an explicit **`score × condition` interaction** test — `~ score_group * condition + (1 | donor_id)` — which formalises the question "is there a gene whose score-dependence is *different* in PD vs HC?" and pulls out the PD-specific subset from the shared cytotoxic-effector axis.
